High-performance computing on SIMD devices, including GPUs, has historically been challenging for object-oriented programming due to alignment and casting issues when allocating memory.  To address this, we have developed DynaSOAr, a novel memory allocator tailored for object-oriented development on SIMD devices.  DynaSOAr enables concurrent memory allocation and management for global memory arrays, allowing for rapid development of high-performance applications.  By leveraging a unique memory layout based on arrays of structures, DynaSOAr eliminates the need for explicit casting and provides a more transparent and efficient memory management system than existing solutions.  We have applied DynaSOAr to create a range of applications, including a matrix library, a sorting algorithm, and a scientific simulation program, and have observed significant performance improvements with DynaSOAr.  Our allocator is now integrated into the CUDA toolkit, making it easily accessible for developers.  Through DynaSOAr, we have also introduced a new memory allocation function called cuSOAAlloc, which provides a more efficient memory layout and has led to further performance gains in certain applications.  We have analyzed the performance benefits of DynaSOAr and cuSOAAlloc, and have found that they result in average speedups of 1.3 to 3.1 times over the standard CUDA allocator.  We have open-sourced DynaSOAr under the permissive BSD-3 license.  In addition to its practical applications, DynaSOAr has also been recognized with the 2020 POPL Best Poster Award and has been featured in a research paper presented at the 2023 Symposium on Programming Languages.  We hope that by sharing our research, we can inspire further innovation in the development of high-performance applications on SIMD devices using object-oriented programming.  Through DynaSOAr, we have demonstrated the potential for object-oriented development on SIMD devices and have shown that the challenges associated with memory access can be overcome with a carefully designed memory allocator.  As a result, we believe that the field of high-performance computing on SIMD devices using object-oriented programming will continue to evolve and thrive in the future. A new theoretical approach has been developed to study the localized spin states of magnetic adatoms and molecules on the surface of a superconducting material. This approach applies the principles of quantum mechanics and applies a minimal parameterization to the problem at hand. The theoretical model includes the adatom or molecule, the underlying crystal lattice, and the electron field that interacts with the spin state of the system. Utilizing this model, a complete picture of the Yu--Shiba--Rusinov states can be achieved through numerical simulation. The developed theory was specifically applied to study the localized spin states of a single manganese atom and manganese pairs on the Niobium (110) surface. Experimental measurements were compared to the predicted outcomes, revealing that the localized spin states can be highly sensitive to the position of the adatom or molecule, and that very small adjustments can significantly impact the orbital alignment, resulting in an experimental identification of a previously theoretical state. The study demonstrates the capability of the theoretical approach to explain the variability of experimental outcomes on different locations on the surface and highlights the importance of a precise description of the underlying crystal lattice and the atomic structure at the location of the spin state formation. The developed theory can be applied to study the localized spin states in the environment of a superconducting host material. The study was conducted in collaboration with the experimental group led by T. Our analysis indicates that substituting oxygen with a p-dopant (C or N) leads to a significant distortion around the dopant and resulting Ti atoms, resulting in increased band gaps compared to undoped TiO2. Conversely, both nitrogen and carbon doped systems exhibit minimal magnetization when doping into interstitial positions. Our results suggest that carbon and nitrogen doped TiO2 could serve as effective photocatalysts for water purification, leveraging their modified electronic properties and potential magnetization. Ultimately, our study provides a theoretical basis for further experimentation to confirm these findings and explore their practical applications.

In neural machine translation, the attention model is now an integral component, enabling controlled exploration of the source language for better translations. However, current attention models can lead to 'attention floods', where the model overemphasizes the start of the source sentence, compromising performance. To address this, we propose a novel look-forward attention mechanism that inhibits the model from focusing excessively on early source sentence elements. Empirical results confirm our mechanism's efficacy, yielding superior performances compared to standard attention models and reduced 'attention floods'. The improved translational coherence and the code are available online. Moreover, an extended version of our model that combines look-forward attention with a reverse attention mechanism delivers state-of-the-art scores on WMT'14 English-German and WMT'14 English-French translation tasks. The implementation is now part of the NMT toolkit, Tensor2Tensor. To avoid 'attention floods', the look-forward attention mechanism modifies the attention weighting function to prohibit the model from considering previous source sentence elements with lower source sentence scores. This modification is achieved by introducing a new compare-and-merge operation, where the model prioritizes the target element over the source sentence score. The proposed mechanism is evaluated on several unsampled and sampled datasets, offering valuable insights into the 'attention floods' phenomenon. The extended reverse attention mechanism is also described, along with the intricate discussion of the experimental results. The paper is a revised and expanded version of the initial work presented at the 2020 Conference of the Association for Computational Linguistics. A blockchain-based smart contract is an automated transaction program, utilized in various cryptocurrencies, that is generated through a process similar to compiling computer code. Nonetheless, unlike software development, smart contract development lacks a systematic approach and utilizes diverse languages, resulting in a lack of refinement types and precise validation during compilation. This deficiency leads to uncertain outcomes and potential vulnerabilities in the program's execution. To address this issue, our project develops a separate validation tool to be integrated into the development cycle of smart contracts, specifically designed for the Tezos blockchain and the Michelson programming language used to create such contracts. This validator identifies errors in the type refinement of smart contracts during compilation, enabling developers to fix issues before deploying their contracts to the Tezos blockchain. Our validation tool is part of a research aimed at introducing refinement types to the Michelson language through a process called static compilation, and is now being developed as a standalone component to explore its effectiveness. Our results show that our method is significantly more efficient in terms of computation time and accurately estimates the optimal payoffs for each sub-scenario, which can be used to guide the behavior of the agents. This research paper focuses on the geometric configuration of an ideal fluid spacetime when the Yamabe flow on its conformal metric reaches a soliton state. We have derived energy estimates from the parabolic equation, resulting in stability conditions for the conformal Ricci-Yamabe soliton. These conditions were then applied to determine the soliton's geometric characteristics, including its potential to contract, expand, or remain steady. We also established that along the soliton's flow, certain vector fields and scalar fields remain constant. As a consequence, we were able to identify the soliton's vector field, and demonstrate that the Yamabe flow's monotonicity or non-monotonicity depends on the sign of the Laplacian of the soliton's potential. Furthermore, we were able to establish conditions for the existence of expanding and contracting solitons, and we obtained a pointwise estimate for the Yamabe flow's solution. The interstellar medium is affected by many features, including scintillation patterns produced by pulsars. By studying the brightness variations of the bright pulsar B1133+16, researchers found certain pattern changes to be consistent across different frequency bands, which indicated the presence of an intervening screen within the interstellar space. Further analysis revealed this screen is likely located near the Sun and is oriented at approximately 45 degrees to the Earth's path. Additionally, its distance can be estimated as being somewhere between 3.6 parsecs and 7.4 parsecs. This screen's effect on scintillation patterns causes a shift in the apparent orientation of the pulsar's spin axis by around 0.6 degrees, which may indicate a need for revision in previous assessments of this phenomenon. By considering the screen's potential impact, the spin axis of the pulsar can be reevaluated as being aligned with a direction in the sky (alpha) of approximately 113.05 degrees. This finding may provide a basis for a more comprehensive understanding of the surrounding interstellar environment. Observations of this phenomenon could be further clarified by studying other luminous pulsars. Furthermore, the discovered screen may offer a new perspective on the structure of the local Milky Way by indicating the presence of a dense region near the Sun. This research also suggests the utilization of scintillometry as a method for mapping the regional interstellar medium. This study focuses on temperate exoplanets with thick atmospheres, utilizing a 2D radiative-convective model to simulate their photochemical processes.
The model indicates that the molecular bonds of species like oxygen, water, and methane break down due to stellar radiation, except when atmospheres are saturated with gas, particularly nitrogen, at concentrations over 10 times Earth's, where the breakdown is slowed, with water and methane bonds persisting longer.
Additionally, the absence of a planetary magnetic field exposes the atmosphere to a broader spectrum of electromagnetic radiation, diminishing the presence of certain species in the atmosphere.
The proposed method also takes into consideration the effects of the star on the planet's atmosphere, accounting for different spectral types.
As a result, the study predicts that certain species, such as CH3Cl and CO, will not appear in the atmospheres of temperate exoplanets under any circumstances.

Lastly, we suggest that the combination of thermodynamics and statistical mechanics is the most effective approach for conveying the idea of negative absolute temperature. Finally, some suggestions are provided to students to explore negative temperature through computational modeling. Characterizing colorectal polyps histology is crucial to determine the need for precise surgical excision and follow-up procedures.  The process of making these determinations is complex and depends on multiple factors including histological features from biopsy samples.  To facilitate deep learning-based approaches that can accurately predict the severity of adenomas from biopsy images, we've created UniToPatho, a comprehensive dataset consisting of 31,744 annotated pixels across 2,042 H&E stained images.  These images represent a broad spectrum of colorectal polyp scenarios including non-neoplastic conditions, adenomas with varying dysplasia levels and carcinomas.  For data preparation and training next-generation deep learning models, UniToPatho is made publicly available for researchers worldwide.  In addition, we've tested our dataset with a state-of-the-art segmentation model and a clinical-based classification approach, achieving outstanding results of 0.903 AUC-ROC for segmentation and 0.894 AUC-ROC for classification respectively.  Further development of UniToPatho and its incorporation into clinical workflows will be explored through ongoing collaborative research efforts between pathologists, surgeons and computer scientists. The dataset is available for download at https://unito.patho.unito.it/ and is also accessible through its GitHub repository along with the code utilized in this study. The constant dissemination of radiology images on the internet poses a threat, allowing unauthorized access to sensitive information. In recent years, the emergence of open-source medical imaging databases on the web has created concerns, as they frequently contain unadjusted extension information allowing for potential illumination adjustments, which may compromise patient anonymity. Existing privacy preservation techniques for medical images are primarily focused on encryption, compressions, and artificial intelligence-based methods, yet none of these have been applied to the recently unveiled Minchest X-ray dataset. We introduce a novel approach to preserve patient anonymity in radiology images by employing a locally applied illumination transformation, combining contrast and brightness modifications. This proposed method enhances the privacy of chest X-rays while maintaining diagnostic capability, as evidenced by a classification accuracy of 94.12% in comparison to 94.30% for unmodified images in a COVID-19 diagnosis task. This novel technique was found to be particularly effective in enhancing privacy for images with visible medical marks. In addition to Minchest, it has been successfully applied to other publicly accessible medical imaging datasets. Our research provides a groundbreaking solution to the anonymization of open-source medical imaging datasets and highlights the necessity of factoring in illumination factors in medical image processing. This new approach has been made available on GitHub for public use. In partnership with the Minchest dataset owners and researchers in the medical imaging community, we have developed a benchmark to assess the anonymity of medical imaging datasets and have identified several promising methods for further improvement. These advancements have resulted in a press release from the dataset owner and potential applications in multiple real-world scenarios. With the increasing presence of medical imaging datasets online, our novel technique provides a crucial solution to the pressing issue of patient anonymity.
